cases.quantity: minutes in flicker on 20 March, home 500 m west of one turbine on the equator
cases.basis: geometry: the rotor's apparent diameter divided by the sun's 15 degrees an hour

cases.quantity: hours a year with the wind always from the north (rotor edge-on to the home)
cases.basis: geometry: a disc seen edge-on casts no shadow on the home

cases.quantity: hours with half the sunshine and running 80 % of the time, over hours with all of both
cases.basis: arithmetic: 0.5 x 0.8

cases.quantity: hours with the rotor always facing the home, over the worst case
cases.basis: geometry: a disc facing the home fills nearly the sphere the worst case assumes

cases.quantity: hours the turbine is stopped to bring the home down to 10 expected hours
cases.basis: arithmetic: expected hours less the budget

cases.quantity: level 500 m from one turbine of 105 dB(A), flat ground
cases.basis: the method's formula written out by hand: spreading, air absorption, ground, reflection near the source

cases.quantity: two equal turbines at one place against one
cases.basis: arithmetic: 10 log10(2)

cases.quantity: energy given up to bring a home 2 dB over the limit within it (modes: 3 dB for 4 %, 6 dB for 12 %)
cases.basis: by hand: the 3 dB mode is enough and costs 4 %

cases.quantity: shortest tree linking the corners of a 1,000 m square
cases.basis: geometry: three sides

cases.quantity: capital recovery factor, 8 % over 25 years
cases.basis: the annuity formula written out by hand

cases.quantity: four 4.5 MW turbines on that square, 60,000 MWh a year
cases.basis: arithmetic by hand from the same inputs

cases.quantity: gross energy a year against the power curve summed over the wind distribution in 0.01 m/s steps
cases.basis: the same curve and Weibull distribution summed by hand, finer than the program's bins
